smells.finding: The two edited artifacts are single ~2200- and ~340-character `imperative` prose strings -- the code equivalent of a very long method body. No test method in the diff exceeds 8 lines.

override.repo_standard: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, Subsystem Rigor: 'Workflow mechanisms and verifiers | strengthened durable system'. A checklist step's `imperative` IS the agent-facing contract for that step; the engine reads it as one field and the corpus ships it as prose.
override.reason: The length is inherent to the artifact's form, not a decomposition failure -- an imperative cannot be extracted into helpers because its only consumer is an LLM reading one field. And this gate moves the metric the right way: 2764 -> 2198 and 911 -> 342 characters. Flagging length on a diff that only shortens would be noise.

smells.finding: The new suite is four classes of 1-3 test methods each; no class grew in the two edited suites.

tests/test_prose_deletions.py ships SpineDeadPathProseAbsent and ExecutePlanDeadPathProseAbsent as two structurally identical classes differing only in (path, step, opening-phrase); a parameterized subTest over a (path, step, opening) table would express the same coverage once. Separately, an `imperative(...)` reader helper now exists in three test modules (test_prose_deletions.py, test_map_contract_wiring.py, test_context_manifest.py) with three signatures. Raised as an OBSERVATION only: the duplication is confined to test scaffolding, is 12 lines, and collapsing it would trade legible per-template failure names for brevity -- a fair call to leave.
No method in the diff reaches predominantly into another object's data; the test helpers read a file they own the path to.
(path, step) travels together twice but is passed as two plain args to one 2-line helper; below the threshold where a value object earns its keep.
The entire new pin is bare `str` constants (SPINE_DEAD_OPENING, DEAD_CLAIMS, SUBSTITUTE_AND_RECORD, OVERLAY_PHRASE) compared with `in` / `count` / `index`.

override.repo_standard: docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md, Evidence And Verification Map: 'Mechanism or workflow behavior change | targeted automated tests plus relevant broader suite'. The thing under test IS literal shipped prose.
override.reason: Wrapping a prose sentinel in a type would put a layer of indirection between the assertion and the exact bytes that must be present or absent, which is the property being pinned. The primitive is the subject matter, not a stand-in for a missing abstraction.

smells.finding: Widest new signature is `imperative(path, step)` -- two parameters.

Deleting ONE prose block required coordinated edits in 5 files (2 templates + 3 test modules) and left 2 further live references untouched (scripts/verify_context_declaration.py module docstring lines 10-11, and docs/superpowers/drills/dogfood-context-paths-absent.md lines 43, 79-80 -- both now quoting text that exists nowhere in the corpus). That is textbook shotgun surgery: one conceptual change, many scattered edit sites, because shipped prose is pinned by phrase sentinels scattered across suites named for other properties. Raised as an OBSERVATION, not a blocker: the implementer found and named both stragglers itself under 'Out-of-scope observations' and correctly declined to edit a historical drill record. The durable fix (a single registry of prose sentinels) is a design question for Triage, not this gate.
No file in the diff is being changed for two unrelated reasons; every hunk serves the one deletion.
Deepest navigation is json.loads(...)['tasks'][step]['imperative'] -- dictionary indexing into a document the test owns, not a chain of object delegations.

Nothing in the diff is built for a hypothetical future caller; the gate is a deletion plus a pin, and the pin asserts only what is true now. The DeclaredConfigRefPathStillNamed class could look speculative but is load-bearing -- it guards a real interaction with test_context_declaration_lint.py.

The two re-pointed sentinels each acquired a 7-9 line block comment explaining what moved and why, and the new suite carries a 30-line module docstring -- a comment-to-code ratio that would ordinarily read as prose compensating for unclear code.

override.repo_standard: skills/_shared/global-everyone.md doctrine that a deviation is NAMED rather than smoothed over, plus the gate's own pre-registered contract in TRIPWIRES.md T4 ('a test asserting its PRESENCE ships alongside the tests asserting the dead prose's absence').
override.reason: These comments do not paper over unclear code -- the assertions are three lines of assertIn. They record WHY a sentinel was re-pointed, which is exactly the provenance a later reader needs to tell 'changed a test to green' from a forced re-point. Deleting them would make the code no clearer and the history unrecoverable. Verified independently: the comments' factual claims hold (both old sentinels occurred exactly once each, only inside the deleted block).
